figures.finding: Rwanda has no rule of its own for child performers: the Labour Law sets employment at sixteen, lets a child of thirteen to fifteen do only light work in the context of apprenticeship (from a list the Minister's order sets), and bars the listed harmful forms of work to anyone under eighteen.

lightWork.only: in the context of apprenticeship; list by Ministerial Order

figures.applies: Rwanda, Law 66/2018 arts. 3, 5, 6. The Ministerial Order listing light works was not read.

sources.said: The minimum age for admission to employment is sixteen (16) years.

However, a child aged between thirteen (13) and fifteen (15) years is allowed to perform only light works in the context of apprenticeship. An Order of the Minister in charge of labour establishes the list of light works for the child

figures.finding: At eighteen a person is fully capable of all civil acts; a minor of sixteen may be emancipated on justified grounds; the guardian represents the minor but may not administer the minor's earnings from an occupation unrelated to the guardian's duties, or what they buy. No share is set aside by law.
figures.applies: Rwanda, Law 32/2016 arts. 113, 114 and the guardian's powers.

sources.said: The age of majority is eighteen (18) years, unless provided otherwise by this Law or other laws. A person having attained that age, is fully qualified for all acts involving civil life.
In case of justifiable grounds, a minor having attained the age of sixteen (16) years may be emancipated
However, the guardian shall not be allowed to administer the minor’s occupational earnings from an activity unrelated to the guardian’s duties, as well as the property acquired through such earnings.
